items.statement: The same argument gives that A{f₁,…,f_n/g} is perfectoid whenever the f_i and g admit compatible systems of p^m-th roots; it is true without that hypothesis, Scholze deducing it by an approximation of f_i, g ∈ A° by elements #f̃_i♭, #g̃♭.

items.name: Uniform products and the Gelfand transform of a perfectoid algebra
items.statement: Uniform products of perfectoid algebras are perfectoid, because (∏A^{αo})/ϖ ≅ ∏(A^{αo}/ϖ). If A is perfectoid so is its Gelfand transform Γ(A), and Γ(A♭) ≅ Γ(A)♭: Γ(A) is a uniform product of the fields ℋ(x), each a uniform colimit of rational localizations of A hence perfectoid, and the second assertion follows from the commutation of rational localizations with tilting together with ℳ(A) ≅ ℳ(A♭). For A not perfectoid, Γ(A)♭ can be much larger than Γ(A♭), as for A = K⟨T⟩.

items.name: K-Perf is complete, and what its limits are
items.statement: The category of perfectoid K-algebras is complete, because K-uBan is complete and K-Perf is coreflective in it. In characteristic p the embedding also has a left adjoint and so reflects limits: perfectoid limits are the uniform limits, and ♭ commutes with ulim. In characteristic 0 one obtains them by tilting: perfectoid limits are ulim^♮.

items.name: Perfectoid limits differ from uniform limits already for finite limits
items.statement: In characteristic 0 perfectoid and uniform limits do not coincide, already for finite limits: the intersection of two perfectoid subalgebras of a perfectoid algebra need not be perfectoid, as Â_∞[√g] = (completion of Q(A_∞))(√g) ∩ Â_∞⟨g^{1/2^∞}⟩ shows for p=2, n=1, g=T+4.

items.name: Invariants under an infinite group need not be perfectoid
items.statement: Proposition 3.8.1 does not extend to infinite groups: the Galois action of Z_p on T₁^{1/p^∞} extends by continuity to Â_∞, but the algebra A₀ of its invariants is not perfectoid.

items.name: The tilt of a perfectoid limit
items.statement: For char K = 0 with ϖ = #(ϖ♭), the perfectoid limit of a projective system of perfectoid K♭-algebras is their uniform limit. For a system of perfectoid K-algebras with uniform limit A, the perfectoid limit is A♮, whose tilt is determined by (A♮)^{♭o} = A^{♭o} = lim_F A° = lim_{F,α}A^{αo} = lim_α A^{α♭o} = lim_{F,α}(A^{αo}/ϖ) (3.17); A♮ → A is not an isomorphism in general.

items.name: A uniform limit of perfectoid algebras that is not perfectoid
items.statement: With p=2, n=1, g=T+4: by Théorème 4.2.2 the uniform limit of the Â_∞⟨g^{1/2^∞}⟩⟨ϖ^j/g⟩ is g^{−1/2^∞}Â_∞⟨g^{1/2^∞}⟩, the complete integral closure of Â_∞⟨g^{1/2^∞}⟩ in its localization at g; passing to 2Z₂-invariants, the uniform limit of the invariants is the complete integral closure of Â_∞[√g] in Â_∞[√g,1/g]. Since Â_∞ is completely integrally closed and the integral closure of a completely integrally closed ring in an algebraic extension of its fraction field is again completely integrally closed, that limit is Â_∞[√g], which is not perfectoid.
items.locator: Exemple prophylactique 3.8.5, p. 52; [8, ch. V, §1, ex. 14]

items.name: K-Perf is cocomplete
items.statement: The category of perfectoid K-algebras has filtered colimits, namely the uniform colimits, since Frobenius stays surjective on colim(B_α^{oa}/ϖ) ≅ (ucolim B_α)^{oa}/ϖ (3.18); having also amalgamated sums ⊗̂^u = ⊗̂, it is cocomplete, colimits being computed as in K-uBan and commuting with tilting.

items.name: Completed algebraic extensions and infinite coproducts
items.statement: The completion of an algebraic extension of a perfectoid field K is the uniform colimit of the finite separable subextensions, each perfectoid, hence perfectoid. The coproduct of a family of perfectoid K-algebras is the completed tensor product ⊗̂_α B_α, and for every perfectoid B the morphism ⊗̂_{α∈B^{♭o}}K⟨T_α^{1/p^∞}⟩ → B, T_α ↦ #α, has dense image.

items.name: The p-adic Riemann extension theorem
items.statement: By the Riemann extension theorem bounded analytic functions on a complex polydisc minus a hypersurface g=0 extend to the polydisc; the p-adic analogue holds: with A = K₀°[[T₁,…,T_n]] = W(k)[[T_{≤n}]] and A₀ = A[1/p], one has A = lim_j A₀{ϖ^j/g}° (4.1) for every non-zero g∈A. Perfectoid versions of this statement are the object of §4.
items.locator: §4, opening, p. 53; [4] Bartenwerfer, quoted without a statement number

items.name: A short proof of the unit-ball form of the extension theorem
items.statement: The weaker statement A = lim_j A₀{ϖ^j/g}_{≤1} (4.2) has a short proof: after a change of variables one may take g in Weierstrass form in T_n, so that A/gA ≅ ⊕_{s<r}K₀°[[T_{<n}]]T_n^s and, by Nakayama, A = ⊕_s K₀°[[T_{<n},g]]T_n^s; applying ⊗_{K⟨g⟩_{≤1}}K⟨g,p^j/g⟩_{≤1} and killing p-primary torsion gives a compatible decomposition of A₀{p^j/g}_{≤1}, which reduces the claim to g = T_n, handled by expanding in powers of T_n. Passing to the uniform colimit to reach the perfectoid algebra Â_∞ "ne va pas de soi"; that is taken up in Exemple 4.2.6, where the equality with A₀{ϖ^j/g}° is also proved.
items.locator: §4.1, formula (4.2), p. 53; [8, VII, §3, n. 7 lemme 3 and n. 8 prop. 5]

items.name: Almost perfectoid envelopes of affinoid algebras
items.statement: Let B be a reduced affinoid K-algebra of dimension n. Choose a Noether normalisation making B a finite extension of A := K⟨T_{≤n}⟩, and choose g ∈ A° such that B[1/g] is étale over A[1/g]. Let 𝒜 be the almost perfectoid algebra g^{−1/p^∞}K⟨T_{≤n}^{1/p^∞},g^{1/p^∞}⟩ and let ℬ be the integral closure of B⊗_A𝒜 in B⊗_A𝒜[1/g]. Then ℬ is almost perfectoid by Proposition 5.3.1, and ℬ^{oa} is finite étale over 𝒜^{oa} modulo every power of p, in the setting (K°[T^{1/p^∞}],(ϖT)^{1/p^∞}K°[T^{1/p^∞}]) via T^{1/p^k} ↦ g^{1/p^k}. If Question 3.5.1 has a positive answer then 𝒜 and ℬ are even perfectoid. This attaches perfectoid algebras to an arbitrary reduced affinoid algebra, where previous constructions were confined to toric situations governed by the logarithmic form of Faltings’ almost purity theorem.
items.note: The hypotheses are choices: the Noether normalisation, and an element g with B[1/g] étale over A[1/g], whose existence the paper does not argue here. The perfectoidness of 𝒜 and ℬ is conditional on Question 3.5.1 (p. 46), which the paper leaves open in characteristic 0. The tensor products are printed uncompleted.

prerequisites.citation: O. Gabber and L. Ramero, Almost ring theory, Lecture Notes in Math. 1800, Springer, 2003 [15]; and Foundations for almost ring theory, arXiv:math/0409584 [16]
prerequisites.why: The most-cited input, 27 occurrences on pp. 1 and 4–8 (the whole of §1) and again on pp. 42–43 and 61: the (V,m) almost setting, Va-modules and Va-algebras (2.2.12), the functors ()_*, ()_! and ()_!! and their adjunctions (2.2.25), almost projective and almost finite modules (2.3.10(i), 2.4.15, 2.4.18, 2.4.28), almost étale and unramified morphisms (3.1.2(vi), 3.2.26(ii)), and almost Galois descent (5.2.1). The arXiv Foundations version is cited separately for th. 6.3.92 and §6.3 on pp. 36–39. André's §1 is a digest of this book, so the roadmap needs the book's statements, not a re-derivation.

prerequisites.why: 17 occurrences on pp. 24–45 and 61–63: uniform Banach algebras and spectral seminorms (2.6.2, 2.8.8, 2.8.16(b)), ℋ(x) as a uniform colimit of rational localisations (2.4.17), perfectoid quotients by closed radicial ideals (3.1.6 d), the tilting equivalence ℳ(A) ≅ ℳ(A♭) (3.3.7), dense-image stability (3.6.17(b)), quotient norms and almost surjectivity on unit balls (3.6.9(c)), and 3.6.5, 3.6.11, 3.6.21, 5.5.9. With [30] this is one of the two sources of the almost-purity theorem the paper extends.

prerequisites.why: 13 occurrences on pp. 1, 7 and 35–43: the definition of perfectoid field and perfectoid algebra (§5, 5.6), tilting (4.10, 4.13, 7.5), the almost purity theorem (th. 7.9) that this paper generalises to the ramified case, rational localisations (def. 2.13, th. 6.3(ii), lem. 6.4(iii)) and the approximation lemma (cor. 6.7(i)).

prerequisites.why: 12 occurrences on pp. 11–13, 22–23, 28 and 68: closedness of maximal ideals (1.2.4/5), the universal property of A⟨T⟩ (1.4.3 cor. 2), the characterisation of multiplicative norms (1.5.3), the non-field example of 1.7.1, 2.1.8 prop. 6, the spectral value of a monic polynomial (3.1.1 prop. 1 and 3.1.2 prop. 1) — which is what formula (2.11) rests on — the uniformity of reduced affinoid algebras (6.2.1), the fact that the algebra determines the topology and the spectral norm (6.1.3 prop. 2), and Noether normalisation (cor. 6.1.2/2), on which the final application §5.4 depends.

prerequisites.why: 6 occurrences on pp. 30–31 and 45: the Berkovich spectrum ℳ(A) and its points as bounded multiplicative seminorms (1.2.3, 1.3.2), the Gelfand transform and the fields ℋ(x) (7.4.2, 9.1, 9.2.3). The spectral seminorm of §2.2 is interpreted through ℳ(A) in footnote 7.

routes.title: Perfectoid rings and spaces, Part II: ramification and Riemann extension
routes.brief:
Extend Perfectoid rings and spaces (PerfectoidSpaces) beyond its unramified P3 theorem, without rebuilding P0 almost mathematics, P1 tilting, P2 rational localization or P8 finite-group invariants. Import the general topological algebra from foundations of adic spaces (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces) and the appropriate tensor-product prefix of Adic spaces, Part II (AdicSpacesPartII), verifying its precise stage ownership before blueprinting. First construct the almost-Banach category for the explicitly specified ramified ideal (ϖT)^(1/p^∞), almost-perfectoid algebras and the right perfectoid coreflection. Do not identify that right adjoint with the prismatic universal perfectoidization of PerfectoidQuotients. Prove André Proposition 4.2.1 with its integral root-localization models, Theorem 4.2.2 identifying lim_j A{ϖ^j/g}° with the intersection g^(-1/p^∞)A°, and its complete-integral-closure assertion. Retain the non-zero-divisor and compatible-root hypotheses. Establish the inverse-limit Frobenius criterion with only the implication directions proved in Proposition 4.3.1; prove Proposition 4.4.1 by its summable annihilator estimates, rather than assuming surjective transition maps. Construct the compatible annular category and Theorem 4.4.2: localization is fully faithful with uniform-limit right adjoint and isomorphic unit, but arbitrary essential surjectivity is not an output. For B′ finite étale over A[1/g], prove all three parts of Proposition 4.4.4 and the recovery B[1/g]≅B′. The final categorical theorem is exactly Theorem 5.2.1: complete A°ᵃ-algebras finite étale modulo every p^m and after inverting g are equivalent, by inverting ϖ, to almost-perfectoid A^â-algebras finite étale after inverting g, and then to finite étale A[1/g]-algebras by inverting g. Prove separately Proposition 5.2.3 in its two different almost bases. Prove the identifications and maximality in Proposition 5.3.1, distinguishing the almost-perfectoid integral envelope D from the largest perfectoid A-algebra D^♮ in B′. State trace almost-surjectivity only when B′ is faithful. Preserve Questions 3.5.1, 4.4.3 and 5.2.2 as boundaries rather than theorem targets. Complete extraction of the source’s §2–3 foundations, examples and §5.4 application before this brief is approved; any general missing construction already owned elsewhere must be imported rather than retained here. The current item list is a checkpoint, not an exhaustive blueprint.

Scope after the third pass (Claude Code, cc-fb70e5). The Part II now carries the whole of the paper that the atlas does not already plan, in four blocks. (i) §2, the bicomplete category K-uBan of uniform Banach K-algebras: the spectral semi-norm and uniformity, the dictionary of Sorite 2.3.1 between uniform Banach algebras and flat ϖ-adically complete K°-algebras with (·)_* = Hom(K°°,−), the almost-elements endofunctor and the corrected left adjoint (·)^!!, the topological almost category A^â-uBan, integral extensions and the invariant-norm lemma 2.4.1, the root saturation g^{−1/p^∞}B° with its six closedness criteria, extremal epimorphisms and uniform rational localization, uniform products and the Gelfand transform, uniform limits and colimits, and the identification of A⟨g^{1/p^∞}⟩ as a colimit of localizations. This block is generic normed-algebra and category theory and the design job must EXPORT it rather than bury it: its long-term home is the Tau Ceti Foundations of adic spaces roadmap (Layer 0 already owns boundedness, A°, A°°, Tate algebras, completion and the open mapping theorem, and Layer 3 the rational localisation), which a source route cannot re-plan. (ii) §3.5–3.9, the parts of the perfectoid category the atlas does not plan: almost perfectoid algebras, K-Perf as a coreflective subcategory with the functor ♮ = ♯∘♭, perfectoid limits as ulim^♮ and the counterexamples separating them from uniform limits, invariants under a finite group of isometries, and the Gelfand transform of a perfectoid algebra. (iii) §4, the perfectoid Riemann extension theorem and the complete integral closure it computes. (iv) §5, the perfectoid Abhyankar lemma itself and the almost perfectoid envelopes of §5.4, whose statement must keep its choices (Noether normalisation, the element g with B[1/g] étale over A[1/g]) and its conditional clause (Question 3.5.1 is open in characteristic 0). Items are stated in corrected form wherever a source issue bites; see sourceIssues E1, E4–E9 and the notes on the items concerned.

sourceIssues.locator: Published §2.2.4, second paragraph, p. 13; the same assertion and proof are in arXiv:1609.00320v1 §2.2.4, p. 12
sourceIssues.printed: On en déduit qu'une K-algèbre A admet au plus une norme spectrale pour laquelle elle est complète : en effet, si || 1, || 2 sont deux telles normes, on peut supposer, en remplaçant la première par le supremum des deux, que le morphisme identique (A,|| 1) → (A,|| 2) est continu. Par le théorème de l'image ouverte de Banach [7, I.3.3, th. 1], || 1 est équivalente à || 2, donc ce morphisme est bicontinu et l'on conclut de ce qui précède que || 1 = || 2.
sourceIssues.correction: The assertion is false as stated. Keep the preceding sentence, which is what the paper actually needs and which is true: the spectral norm of a uniform normed algebra is the unique spectral norm compatible with its topology. A completeness variant must add a hypothesis making the two norms comparable — for instance that the identity is continuous in one direction, or that the maximum of the two is complete.
sourceIssues.reason: Take K = Q_p and A = C_p as an abstract Q_p-algebra. Choose t in a transcendence basis B of C_p over the algebraic closure F of Q_p; since F(pt) = F(t), the set (B∖{t}) ∪ {pt} is again a transcendence basis, so there is a field automorphism σ of C_p over F with σ(t) = pt. Then |x|' := |σ(x)| is again a multiplicative Q_p-algebra norm, and (C_p,|·|') is complete because σ is an isometric bijection onto (C_p,|·|); but |t|' = |pt| = p^{-1}|t| ≠ |t|. So C_p carries two distinct complete spectral — indeed multiplicative — norms. The step that fails is the replacement of ||1 by the supremum: for a_n ∈ F converging to t for |·|, one has |a_n − x|' = |a_n − σ(x)|, so the same sequence converges to σ^{-1}(t) = p^{-1}t for |·|'; it is Cauchy for the maximum of the two norms and has two different limits, so the maximum is not complete and the open mapping theorem does not apply to it. Downstream audit (every occurrence of the assertion in the paper is on pp. 13, 22 and 41): it is USED once, in the proof of Lemme 2.4.1(2) p. 22 — « Notons par ailleurs que si la norme est spectrale complète, elle est unique avec cette propriété (cf. 2.2.2), donc préservée par G » — and the counterexample above is exactly of that shape, a non-continuous automorphism moving the norm. That use is repairable by the paper's own part (3): γ(b) satisfies the same monic polynomial ∏_{γ∈G}(T−γ(b)) ∈ A[T] as b, whose coefficients determine the spectral value by [6, 3.1.2, prop. 1], so |·|_sp is G-invariant for that reason. On p. 41 the assertion is invoked for the perfectoidness of a finite étale extension, but the valid reason — uniqueness of the spectral norm compatible with the canonical topology of a finite projective module — is given in the same parenthesis. No main theorem is affected.

sourceIssues.printed: Les produits infinis d'algèbres de Banach n'existent pas en général : si A n'est pas uniforme et si a_n est une suite non bornée d'éléments de A^o, la donnée des morphismes K --1↦a_n--> A ne peut équivaloir à celle d'un morphisme de K vers une algèbre de Banach.
sourceIssues.correction: The source of the test morphisms is the free object K⟨T⟩, with T ↦ a_n, and likewise « un morphisme de K⟨T⟩ vers une algèbre de Banach ».
sourceIssues.reason: A unital K-algebra homomorphism K → A sends 1 to 1, so the morphisms described do not exist unless a_n = 1. What makes the argument work is the free object of §2.1.5 and §2.5.1, for which Hom(K⟨T⟩,A) = A°; the unbounded sequence then gives a family of morphisms that no single Banach algebra can corepresent.
